The bug is `chunk(100)` using offset pagination while each processed row is removed from the `WHERE backfilled_at IS NULL` result set. After the first 100 rows are stamped, the next query applies `OFFSET 100` to the now-smaller set, skipping the next 100 rows. This repeats across chunks, leaving many orders unprocessed.
The smoke tests pass because they never exceed one chunk. Replace `chunk(100)` with `chunkById(100)` (or `eachById`), which advances using the stable primary key rather than offsets. It preserves bounded memory and resumability.
<diagnosis>
The command mutates the same filtered dataset that Laravel's offset-based `chunk()` paginates. Stamping rows removes them from the NULL set, so later offsets skip rows—typically processing alternating chunks only. Use `chunkById(100)` ordered by the stable `id` column; after each batch it fetches rows with `id > last_id`, so updates cannot shift later pages, while memory remains bounded and reruns process only rows still missing `backfilled_at`.
</diagnosis>
